sources.reference: User-supplied annotated ILCA diagram (2026-10-07), showing the rudder head, gudgeon, pintle, tiller retaining pin and rudder downhaul. Used only to identify hardware and relative arrangement, not as a dimensioned survey.
sources.blade: VISUAL ESTIMATE: symmetric elliptical foil cross-sections, 32 perimeter samples, height fractions, small rounded leading tip and rounded thickness run-out. Existing data/laser.json rudder chord 0.203 m, maximum thickness 0.020 m, immersed span 0.527 m, leading-edge position, tip radius and 12-degree leading-edge rake remain the dimensions; the rounded tip stays inside their planform envelope. The visible top still uses half the existing visual head height. This is not a hydrodynamic foil-section claim.
sources.head: VISUAL ESTIMATE: all cheek thicknesses, corner radii, bevels, bridge proportions, head bottom, fastener locations and finish colours. Existing visual head width/length/height locate the cheek silhouette and blade pivot; the opening separates two shaped cheeks rather than painting a slot on a solid box.
sources.hardware: VISUAL ESTIMATE: all mount, plate, gudgeon, pintle, bushing, bolt, washer, retaining-pin and ring dimensions, tessellation and mount elevations. Two fixed transom gudgeons support coaxial rotating pintles, with a real hole around each pintle. Render-only mounts do not alter stock location or steering axis. Matte roughness 0.86 and metalness 0 are rendering choices, not material specifications.
sources.tiller: VISUAL ESTIMATE: all tiller section, rounded-corner, taper, bent-root, socket, grip and attachment proportions. Existing tiller length and layout.tillerZ remain exact; the end-joint centre matches layout.tillerEnd at every steering angle.
sources.downhaul: VISUAL ESTIMATE: all downhaul radii, anchor/guide/cleat positions and tail length; a restrained static taut line from the blade to a tiller cleat. The line and all its attachments rotate together, without crossing to a hull-fixed endpoint. No raise/lower animation, rope tension or control simulation is introduced.
sources.simulation: All fields in this file are render-only. No class/simulator hull, foil, stock or control dimensions, inputs, TS/Go forces or steering conventions change. Daggerboard geometry and finish are unchanged. Geometry, vertex colours and smoothed normals are baked once per boat, with per-boat owned resources and no per-frame mesh rebuilding.
